newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Superquinn plans bid for ABF's Irish stores.
newsitem.headline: Superquinn plans bid for ABF's Irish stores.

text.p: Privately-owned Irish supermarket group Superquinn said on Friday that it was interested in bidding for Associated British Foods' Irish stores and did not think it had left it too late.

ABF is currently in talks with British supermarket group Tesco Plc about the sale of its Quinnsworth/Crazy Prices Group in the Republic of Ireland and its Northern Irish supermarket interests, Stewarts and Crazy Prices.
Irish media reports said on Friday that a deal was close to completion and could be announced as early as today.
Tesco is expected to pay over 600 million sterling ($955.7 million) for the stores which are market leaders on both sides of the border.

But Superquinn chairman Feargal Quinn told Irish state radio that he didn't think his group had left it too late to make an offer as ABF was a public company and would have to consider any bid put to them.
"It seems to be that such a large amount of a deal could not go ahead without, from the shareholder's point of view, taking account of the highest bidder," he said.

He said Superquinn did not move earlier to bid for the ABF stores, which have a 26 percent market share in the Republic of Ireland and a 30 percent share in Northern Ireland, as it did not believe that sufficient money would be available to such a small company.
Superquinn is the smallest of the Irish supermarket chains with 16 shops in the Republic of Ireland. It is 90 percent owned by Quinn's family.

"Quite truthfully, we are a small company. We have 3,000 employees but Quinnsworth and Crazy Prices have 7,000 so we really didn't include it in our options that we would be able to take over the total company north and south," Quinn, a cousin of Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn, said.

"It was only when we read in the papers what was happening and we were approached by our financial advisers who said there is enough money, you could do it, you are held in very high regard by the banking fraternity and on that basis if you want to put a package together it can be put together."
Quinn said he hoped the talks between Tesco and ABF broke down today which would allow Superquinn into the bidding but even if they came to a conclusion, Superquinn would still be interested.

If Superquinn succeeded in acquiring the ABF stores, it would ideally turn some of Quinnsworth shops into Superquinns and hold that as a family company while selling off the Stewarts stores in Northern Ireland to the highest bidder.
"We would move the Crazy Prices stores into a different company, in competition with Superquinn but hopefully Irish-owned, Irish institutional money in competition with us," Quinn said.
